title: Quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization
abstract: We introduce a quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization. Quantum dynamics based on quantum annealing (QA) or the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is used to engineer the transition kernel. Increasing the annealing time in QA or the number of layers in QAOA enables transitions to explore distant configurations while suppressing large energy changes. The Hamming-space delocalization originates from operator spreading, whereas the energy-space localization arises from a dynamically generated correlation. For optimization, we propose quantum-echo local optimization with and without greedy descent. We find that its performance is governed by the interplay between Hamming-space nonlocality and energy-space locality, and that excessive energy-space localization can degrade optimization performance. Incorporating greedy descent substantially improves the performance, highlighting the complementary roles of quantum dynamics for exploration and greedy descent for exploitation. These results establish quantum-echo dynamics as a framework for engineering structured transition kernels and provide a route to using finite-resource quantum many-body dynamics as a computational primitive for iterative optimization.
summary: This work introduces a quantum-echo Markov process to tackle combinatorial optimization by engineering structured transition kernels using QA or QAOA. The key insight is that optimal performance requires a balance between quantum exploration (Hamming nonlocality) and controlled energy changes (energy locality). The framework shows that combining this quantum process with classical greedy descent significantly boosts optimization capability.
main_problem: The paper develops and analyzes a quantum-echo Markov process designed to efficiently explore the configuration space of combinatorial optimization problems.
main_result: The performance of the optimization hinges on balancing Hamming-space nonlocality (for exploration) and energy-space locality (for suppressing large energy jumps), with greedy descent providing crucial exploitation.
method: The process uses quantum dynamics from QA or QAOA to engineer a transition kernel, characterized by analyzing locality in both Hamming and energy spaces.
model_or_system: The model applies to general combinatorial optimization problems, using a cost function $C_z$ on binary spin configurations $z$. The dynamics are governed by quantum annealing (QA) or QAOA circuits.
key_observables: Hamming-space locality ($d_H$), Energy-space locality ($d_E$), and the effective indicator ($\xi$) quantifying energy-space correlation.
important_parameters: Annealing time ($	au$) or QAOA layers ($p$), which control the degree of quantum evolution and thus the locality structure.
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the finite-resource regime, and various approximations (like Random-Phase Approximation) are used to calculate expectation values.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates desired move types: nonlocal in Hamming space but local in energy space, contrasting with trapped or purely random moves.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the quantum-echo process, defines locality measures in both spaces, analyzes how QA/QAOA dynamics generate specific locality structures, and finally proposes and evaluates the combined quantum-echo local optimization with greedy descent.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete framework for using finite-resource quantum dynamics to engineer structured transition kernels for optimization, linking quantum dynamics directly to classical search heuristics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic illustration of three types of moves gen- erated by a transition matrix. The circle denotes the current configuration, and the shaded region represents the candidate configurations. Hamming-local moves can be trapped in a lo- cal minimum, whereas moves that are nonlocal in both Ham- ming and energy spaces effectively approach random sam- pling. The desired transitions are nonlocal in the Hamming space but local in the energy space, allowing the search to escape local minima without inducing large energy changes.

FIG. 2. Energy-space locality dE versus Hamming-space locality dH for (a) the random Ising model and (b) the REM. Solid lines show the exact dE, whereas dotted lines and dashed lines represent approximations drpa E and dcw E , respectively. Squares (red) and circles (blue) denote the quantum-echo Markov process based on QA and QAOA, respectively, and triangles (black) denotes the random up-to-k spin flips. Arrows indicate increasing p, τ, and k. In the REM, both approximations closely reproduce the exact result, whereas in the random Ising model, a deviation between dE and drpa E appears for small τ and p. We set N = 12 for both models.
